title: OpenAI for VP's of AI + Advice for Building Agents
talk_summary: An OpenAI go-to-market talk that spends its first half on enterprise AI adoption phases and a Morgan Stanley RAG case study, then pivots to four agent-building lessons from OpenAI's field experience. The actionable core is: build with primitives before frameworks, start with a single agent before multi-agent networks, use handoffs to swap model/prompt/tools while preserving context, and run guardrails in parallel rather than inside the main prompt.

takeaways.what_they_do: Build agents with raw API calls, logging inputs/outputs/failures first, so you understand task decomposition and failure points; only introduce abstraction when you catch yourself reimplementing the same thing (embedding strategy, model graders).
takeaways.evidence_quote: start simple optimize when needed and Abstract only when it makes your system better

takeaways.technique: Single agent first, graduate to network on observed failures
takeaways.what_they_do: Ship one purpose-built single-task agent to a limited user set, observe real bottlenecks (hallucination, latency, poor retrieval), then add complexity only for discovered failure cases.
takeaways.evidence_quote: complexity as something which increases as we discover more intense failure cases and constraints

takeaways.technique: Handoffs that swap model/prompt/tools while keeping context
takeaways.what_they_do: Route sub-tasks to different models by role: cheap mini model for triage, mid model for conversation, reasoning model for accuracy-sensitive checks, passing full conversation history across the handoff.
takeaways.evidence_quote: using a GPD 40 mini call to perform triage ... using a O3 mini reasoning model to perform accuracy sensitive tasks

takeaways.technique: Parallel guardrails outside the main prompt
takeaways.what_they_do: Keep the main prompt focused on the happy path; run input guardrails (e.g. prompt injection) and output guardrails as separate parallel calls on fast cheap models, deferring high-stakes actions until all guardrails return.
takeaways.evidence_quote: guardrails should not necessarily be made part of your main prompts but should instead be run in parallel

takeaways.technique: Simple focused prompts, edge cases to guardrails
takeaways.what_they_do: Keep model instructions short and targeted at the task so accuracy can be hill-climbed predictably; move edge-case handling out of the prompt into guardrail calls.
takeaways.evidence_quote: keeping the model instructions simple and focused on the target task ensures maximum interoperability

takeaways.technique: Define success metrics before development, iterate methods
takeaways.what_they_do: Morgan Stanley case: started at 45% accuracy, added hybrid retrieval, fine-tuning, chunking, reranking, classification, prompt engineering and query expansion to reach 98% against a 90% goal.
takeaways.evidence_quote: accuracy was pretty bad to start right it was 45% ... we got to 98% accuracy
